summary.text: NIST released its AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) in January 2023 as voluntary guidance for organizations designing, developing, deploying, or using AI systems to manage AI risks. NIST described the framework as flexible and measurable, intended to adapt as AI technologies develop, and said it planned periodic updates with the AI community. NIST launched a public working group on generative AI and, through CAISI, published evaluations of PRC-developed models including DeepSeek and Kimi K2 Thinking. In August 2024 NIST said the U.S. AI Safety Institute signed agreements giving it access to major new models before and after public release for collaborative safety research, and in 2026 it announced an AI Agent Standards Initiative.

statements.text: The U.S. Department of Commerce’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has released its Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), a guidance document for voluntary use by organizations designing, developing, deploying or using AI systems to help manage the many risks of AI technologies.

statements.text: The framework is part of NIST’s broad and growing portfolio of AI-related work that includes fundamental and applied research along with a focus on measurement and evaluation, technical standards, and contributions to AI policy.

statements.text: The Public Working Group on Generative AI will help address the opportunities and challenges associated with AI that can generate content, such as code, text, images, videos and music. statements.text: The U.S. Department of Commerce’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has released its Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) , a guidance document for voluntary use by organizations designing, developing, deploying or using AI systems to help manage the many risks of AI technologies.

attribution.speaker: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The AI RMF follows a direction from Congress for NIST to develop the framework and was produced in close collaboration with the private and public sectors. It is intended to adapt to the AI landscape as technologies continue to develop, and to be used by organizations in varying degrees and capacities so that society can benefit from AI technologies while also being protected from its potential harms.

attribution.speaker: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The AI RMF provides a flexible, structured and measurable process that will enable organizations to address AI risks. Following this process for managing AI risks can maximize the benefits of AI technologies while reducing the likelihood of negative impacts to individuals, groups, communities, organizations and society.

attribution.speaker: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: NIST plans to work with the AI community to update the framework periodically and welcomes suggestions for additions and improvements to the playbook at any time.

attribution.speaker: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: NIST is committed to continuing its work with companies, civil society, government agencies, universities and others to develop additional guidance.

statements.text: Motivated by federal directive , the report examines the unique challenges of managing super intelligence (SI) incidents, including cybersecurity attacks that target SI systems as well as harms that arise from misuse, malfunction, or unintended actions.
